testPolicy.text: TCU is test-optional, with a 'Do No Harm' policy: if a submitted score would harm the likelihood of admission or scholarship, TCU excludes it from consideration. Self-reported scores are accepted.

cost.totalIncludes: on campus, fall 2026 and spring 2027, 12-18 hours: tuition 66,520 + Student Government Association fee 90 + housing and food 18,780 (typical first-year housing 12,080 + basic meal plan 6,700) + books and supplies 700 = published direct cost 86,090; plus indirect travel 1,374 + personal 2,278 + average loan fees 68. The page gives no grand total; 89,810 is the sum of its published lines. International students add health insurance 2,846.

aidPromise.text: TCU for Texans: first-year fall applicants who are Texas residents and Pell Grant eligible with a family adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less (assuming reasonable assets) may receive full tuition coverage, additional food and housing assistance and guaranteed on-campus housing for four years; it does not cover fees and books. Applicants must complete the Early Action application, FAFSA and CSS Profile by November 1 for full consideration.

deadlines.early: November 1 (EA, non-binding decision by January 1; ED I, binding decision by January 1, commit by January 15)
deadlines.ed2: February 1 (decision by March 1, commit by March 15)

facts.text: Early Decision admitted 935 of 1,373 applicants for fall 2025 (CDS C21), against 10,906 admits from 22,680 applicants overall.

Texans and out-of-state students apply in equal numbers but out-of-state applicants are admitted more often: 4,663 of 10,757 Texas applicants versus 5,818 of 10,483 out-of-state applicants in fall 2025.

TCU for Texans covers full tuition plus food and housing help for Pell-eligible Texas residents with family AGI of $100,000 or less, but only if they apply Early Action and file the FAFSA and CSS Profile by November 1.
Chancellor's Scholars candidates should apply to TCU by November 1 and to the John V. Roach Honors College by November 15.
Under the 'Do No Harm' policy, a submitted SAT or ACT score that would lower an applicant's chances is excluded from review.
For international applicants TCU is need-aware: those who can contribute at least $40,000 a year are the most competitive for admission.

notes: C1 totals are sums: applied 8,705 men + 13,975 women = 22,680; admitted 3,868 + 7,038 = 10,906; enrolled 1,014 + 1,740 = 2,754; they match the residency table totals. CDS C21 ED counts are captioned 'For the Fall 2025 entering class'. CDS C21/C22 dates: ED I 11/1 (notification 1/1), ED II 2/1 (3/15 in the CDS; the admissions page says decision by March 1), EA 11/1 (1/1), not restrictive; C14 closing date 2/1, priority 1/1. C11-C12 GPA sections are blank (all 0.00%), so gpa is null. Contradiction: the testing policy page says the middle 50% of students entering in fall 2026 scored 1310-1460 SAT and 29-33 ACT, while the CDS 2025-26 C9 for fall 2025 enrolled students gives SAT 1110-1330 and ACT 26-31; the CDS values are recorded and the page figure refers to a different year. CDS Part G (2026-27) matches the financial aid page (tuition 66,520, fees 90, food and housing 18,780). G4 says 34% of full-time undergraduates pay more than the G1 tuition and fees (program fees, for example Neeley School of Business). A TCU news release of 2025 gave a $70,000 AGI threshold; the current program page says $100,000, which is recorded.
